use_case: Electric load-forecasting model: hourly day-ahead and 7-day system and substation load forecasts for wholesale purchases, peak-day operating plans, and storm staffing
business_owner: Electric Utility manager of power supply and load forecasting
vendor_or_model: In-house gradient-boosted ensemble (replaced the 2019 regression model in 2025), built on the group data platform (SYS-E6)
data_categories: Substation load history from SCADA historians; AMI interval data aggregated to substation level (no individual customer records); weather forecasts from a commercial feed; calendar; rooftop solar estimates
affects_individuals: No (grid-level; indirect effect on customers through operating plans and costs)
human_in_the_loop: Forecasting analysts review every forecast; the power supply manager approves day-ahead purchases; the DCC approves peak-day operating plans; no automatic control action
applicable_laws: No AI-specific federal or state rule identified. Outside NERC CIP scope (not a BES Cyber System; TCC operations planning uses RC and BA forecasts). Purchase costs may be examined in state cost recovery proceedings (general utility regulation). Guidance: NIST AI RMF 1.0; NIST concept note for an AI RMF Critical Infrastructure Profile (2026-04-07)
